name: Sarvam-105B-1711

lineage.how_derived: further post-training of Sarvam-105B for tool calling, instruction following, agentic tasks and Indian languages; this repo is the NVFP4 build of the BF16 checkpoint sarvam-105b-1711-bf16

purpose: The builder says it improves Sarvam-105B on tool calling, instruction following, agentic tasks and Indian languages; its own benchmark suite is aimed at chat, tools, agents and Indic-language quality.

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card tag apache-2.0 on both repos; no LICENSE file in the repo (404 on raw/main/LICENSE, 2026-11-19), so the text was not read.

architecture.kind: MoE with multi-head latent attention (config model_type sarvam_mla)
architecture.drafter: DSpark speculative decoding documented for vLLM (5 draft tokens)
architecture.why_this_design: The card gives no architecture reasons; it gives vLLM hosting and DSpark throughput recipes only. Context 131,072 is the evaluated window, config max positions is 163,840.

variants.notes: NVFP4 is a Blackwell-native format; the card benchmarks it against BF16 (small loss)

pc-12gb.notes: 70 GB NVFP4 against 9.6 GB VRAM plus about 50 GB RAM; a 4-bit GGUF would be about 60 GB, borderline and slow

pc-16gb.notes: about 4-bit 105B needs roughly 60 to 70 GB; 13.6 GB VRAM + 50 GB RAM does not hold NVFP4 (70 GB); needs a smaller quant, none found

pc-24gb.notes: 21.6 GB VRAM budget + about 70 GB RAM at 96 GB machines holds 70 GB, experts stream from RAM (10.3 B active makes decode RAM-bound)

pc-32gb.notes: 29.6 GB VRAM budget + 128 GB RAM; NVFP4 needs a runtime that reads it (vLLM 0.33 per the card); on a non-NVIDIA GPU a GGUF requant is needed

mac-64gb+.notes: 70 GB against about 52 GB GPU share; only a quant below 4 bits could fit a 64 GB Mac, larger Macs fit

engine_support.notes: Custom MLA MoE architecture 'sarvam_mla'; no GGUF found; NVFP4 repo is for NVIDIA Blackwell stacks.

benchmarks.name: Decode speed, one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB), 1 user, DSpark

strengths: Instruction following and tool-calling scores at or above Gemma-4-31B in the builder's own runs
Strong Indian-language quality against Western open models (vendor suite)
Vendor evaluation is documented in detail: same harness and settings for all models, grader and judge named
weaknesses: Behind Gemma-4-31B on coding, math and BrowseComp in the vendor table
NVFP4 loses visibly on BrowseComp (35.0 against 41.4)
All numbers are the builder's own runs, with an internal Indic suite and LLM judges
soft.behavior: Thinking on by default (temperature 1.0 recommended with thinking, 0.6 without); thinking can be turned off per request with chat_template_kwargs.
best_for: Indian-language assistants and tool-calling agents on a workstation class machine
avoid_for: 16 GB GPU machines without a smaller quant
soft.maturity: Sarvam AI is an Indian lab shipping the 105B and a 30B class; the repo is four days old (327 downloads of the BF16 repo), no discussions.

tona_fit.reason: 105B-A10B with 128 GB of RAM fits only the biggest class, and the strength is Indic languages and tool calling, not coding. The MLA MoE architecture would be new work for Tona. No smaller quant exists yet.

open_questions: GGUF or other quants for non-NVIDIA GPUs
License text and the base model sarvam-105b release date
How MLA and 128 experts are laid out compared with 'sarvam-105b' (the earlier release)
